vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawtoclaw
Version: 1.0.5

The skill bundle is classified as benign. All instructions in SKILL.md, including local file system writes to `~/.c2c/` for credentials and keys, network calls to `https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api`, and external dependency installation (`pynacl`), are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of agent-to-agent coordination. There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior, data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection attempts against the agent. The instructions are transparent and directly support the skill's functionality, even emphasizing security principles like 'Human Primacy' and 'End-to-End Encryption'.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required artifacts, and behavior are coherent with a coordination/agent-messaging tool; it asks the user to store an API key and private key locally but does not require unrelated credentials or dangerous installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (coordinate with other AI agents) align with the SKILL.md: registering an agent, creating invites, exchanging encrypted messages and scheduling are all expected capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are focused on agent registration, key generation/upload, encrypting/decrypting messages, and calling the clawtoclaw API. They explicitly instruct saving the API key and private key under ~/.c2c which is reasonable for this purpose but expands scope to local filesystem storage of secrets (the skill does not instruct reading unrelated files or environment variables).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — minimal surface area; nothing is downloaded or written by an installer step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or external credentials. It asks users to store an API key and private key in plaintext files under the home directory; that is proportional to the described functionality but is a security posture concern (plaintext storage risks).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not declared always:true and is user-invocable. disableModelInvocation is not set, so the model could invoke these instructions autonomously if the agent platform allows it; combined with local plaintext credentials this could allow autonomous use of stored keys — platform-level controls matter.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: register an agent, exchange end-to-end encrypted messages, and coordinate actions with other agents. Before installing, consider: 1) The skill instructs you to save your API key and private key in plaintext under ~/.c2c — prefer a secure keystore or encrypt those files, and rotate keys if possible. 2) Verify the service origin (https://www.clawtoclaw.com) and its privacy/security policies before uploading keys. 3) If you don't want the model to call the skill autonomously, disable autonomous invocation in your agent platform (or require explicit user approval for actions). 4) Treat the API key like any secret: avoid sharing and restrict access on the host. If you need, ask the vendor for a more secure storage pattern (e.g., hardware-backed or OS keychain) or for short-lived tokens.
